questions.tag: United States of America · Central banking
questions.q: What is an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve?
o: An increase in the cost of borrowing money, which makes loans more expensive.
A government tax on corporate profits that lowers stock prices.
A reduction in the total amount of U.S. dollars in global circulation.
A subsidy paid to commercial banks to help them lower consumer loan rates.
questions.e: An interest rate hike raises the cost of borrowing, which ripples through corporate balance sheets and consumer loans. It is like the interest on a loan becoming more expensive. It does not represent a direct tax or a reduction in currency supply.

questions.q: Why did equity valuations in the S&P 500 adjust lower?
o: The central bank's tightening move compressed risk appetite.
A total of 22 companies went bankrupt on Wednesday.
The U.S. Dollar Index fell below the 100 mark.
Corporate tax rates were doubled by the Federal Open Market Committee.
questions.e: Equities retreated across the S&P 500 because the central bank's tightening move compressed risk appetite, leading to 22 constituents printing fresh lows. Bankruptcy and tax changes are not mentioned in the source.

questions.q: What happened to the FTSE 100 index on 17 September 2026?
o: It opened 0.88% higher as European markets turned green.
It fell by 0.88% because sterling depreciated sharply.
It was suspended by the Bank of England ahead of a rate decision.
It closed lower than the Frankfurt stock exchange.
questions.e: The FTSE 100 index opened 0.88% higher on 17 September 2026 as European markets turned green. It did not fall, nor was it suspended.

questions.q: What was the market expectation for the Bank of England's interest rate decision on 17 September 2026?
o: An unchanged interest rate stance.
A sharp rate hike matching the Federal Reserve.
An emergency rate cut to support sterling.
The abolition of the benchmark lending rate.
questions.e: Market participants priced in an unchanged interest rate stance from the Bank of England on 17 September 2026. This meant borrowing costs were expected to remain steady, contrasting with the Federal Reserve.

questions.q: How did the DAX Index open in Frankfurt trading?
o: It opened 0.77% higher following overseas rate adjustments.
It opened 1.6% lower due to a plunge in Brenntag shares.
It remained completely flat throughout the trading session.
It dropped sharply following Bilfinger's market entry.
questions.e: The DAX Index opened 0.77% higher in Frankfurt trading following overseas rate adjustments. Brenntag actually had a prior session gain of 1.6%, rather than causing the index to fall.

questions.q: What happened to Bilfinger shares during the Frankfurt trading session?
o: They plunged against the broader market trend.
They rose by 1.6% alongside Brenntag stock.
They secured the number 2 market share position domestically.
They were acquired by Feike Investment for 900 million yuan.
questions.e: Bilfinger shares plunged against the broader market trend while Frankfurt stocks advanced at the open. The 1.6% gain belonged to Brenntag, and the Chinese acquisitions belong to a different country.

questions.q: What risk did a dovish rate hike pose to the Japanese yen?
o: It risked pushing the yen past the 158 level and testing 160.
It risked strengthening the yen below the 100 mark.
It threatened to replace the yen with the U.S. dollar.
It caused household assets to drop below 2,519 trillion yen.
questions.e: A dovish rate hike by the Bank of Japan risked pushing the yen past the 158 level and testing 160. Household assets actually reached a record peak during this period.

questions.q: Why did Japanese household assets reach a record 2,519 trillion yen?
o: On rising stocks as the Nikkei 225 closed up 0.53%.
Because the Bank of Japan lowered interest rates to zero.
Due to a massive influx of foreign direct investment from China.
As a direct result of the 60% headcount reduction in Risen Energy.
questions.e: Japanese household assets reached a record 2,519 trillion yen on rising stocks, with the Nikkei 225 closing up 0.53%. The other options are either factually incorrect or belong to different markets.

questions.q: What challenge did Calterah face while pursuing its STAR Market IPO?
o: It carried cumulative losses of 900 million yuan.
It reduced its workforce by over 60% in 3 years.
It had to pay 2 billion yuan in short-term debt maturing in 249 days.
It lost control of Shanghai Yahong to Li Gaiteng.
questions.e: Calterah pursued a STAR Market IPO while carrying cumulative losses of 900 million yuan. Risen Energy was the company that reduced its headcount by over 60%, not Calterah.

questions.q: Why did China broaden its yuan foreign exchange clearing capabilities?
o: In a deliberate push for wider global currency adoption.
To bail out Calterah and Risen Energy from cumulative losses.
To replace the domestic stock market with a digital currency.
To prevent Feike Investment from acquiring Shanghai Yahong.
questions.e: China broadened yuan foreign exchange clearing in a deliberate push for wider global currency adoption and internationalisation metrics. It was not a bailout for specific energy or tech firms.

questions.q: What action did the Reserve Bank of India take against 5 non-banking financial companies?
o: It revoked their registration certificates under Section 45-IA (6) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
It provided them with a ₹28,000 crore bailout package.
It forced them to merge with Caitong Securities.
It lowered their reverse repo auction rate to 5.24%.
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India revoked the registration certificates of 5 non-banking financial companies under Section 45-IA (6) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The other options mix up separate government auctions or unrelated Chinese firms.

questions.q: What was the outcome of the Reserve Bank of India's overnight variable rate reverse repo auction on September 17, 2026?
o: It absorbed ₹2,39,959 crore, which fell short of the ₹3,00,000 crore notified amount.
It successfully raised ₹28,000 crore for government security underwriting.
It cancelled all 13 non-banking financial company registrations.
It pushed the benchmark interest rate up to 13.75%.
questions.e: The overnight variable rate reverse repo auction absorbed ₹2,39,959 crore from the banking system, where total bids fell short of the ₹3,00,000 crore notified amount. The 13.75% rate belongs to Brazil's Selic rate.

questions.q: What did Brazil's Copom do to the Selic rate in its fifth consecutive easing action?
o: It reduced the Selic rate to 13.75%.
It increased the benchmark rate to match the Federal Reserve.
It left borrowing costs unchanged at 1 percent.
It replaced the Selic rate with a diesel subsidy mechanism.
questions.e: The Copom reduced the Selic rate to 13.75% in its fifth consecutive easing action to stimulate economic activity during a slowdown. It did not raise rates or replace the benchmark with a subsidy.

questions.q: How did Petrobras handle the diesel price increase of 1 real per liter for distributors?
o: It introduced a subsidy mechanism granting an equivalent discount to neutralize immediate retail spikes.
It passed the entire cost increase directly to citizens without any intervention.
It halted all crude supplies to domestic refineries permanently.
It devalued the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar.
questions.e: Petrobras implemented a diesel price increase while simultaneously introducing a subsidy mechanism granting an equivalent discount to cushion the impact and neutralize immediate retail spikes through corporate discounting.

questions.q: Why did Saudi Aramco suspend crude shipments to Indian refiners?

Because Houthi forces bought all European oil cargoes.
To protest against the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike.
As part of a deliberate push for wider global currency adoption.
questions.e: Saudi Aramco suspended crude shipments to Indian refiners following a key pipeline disruption and missile and drone strikes. The other options are incorrect or unrelated causes.

questions.q: What happened to the naira at the official market?
o: It weakened against the US dollar by 56 kobo.
It strengthened by 50% following fuel price subsidies.
It was officially pegged to the Brazilian Selic rate.
It replaced the US dollar as the primary reserve currency.
questions.e: The naira weakened against the US dollar by 56 kobo at the official market, even though softer consumer prices led to expectations of lower borrowing costs. It was not pegged to Brazil's rate or replaced.

questions.q: How did the S&P/ASX Financials index perform following the US rate action?
o: It added 1.0% to outpace the wider market, bolstered by an upgrade to NAB.
It plunged by 4.35% alongside Metallium and Bellevue Gold.
It remained flat while gold stocks surged to record highs.
It dropped by 0.40% as large-cap stocks led a market-wide sell-off.
questions.e: The S&P/ASX Financials index added 1.0% to outpace the wider market, bolstered by an upgrade to NAB. Gold stocks like Metallium and Bellevue Gold suffered losses, but financials rallied.

o: They suffered sharp losses, with Bellevue Gold trading down to AUD 1.54.
They surged by 1.0% alongside the S&P/ASX Financials index.
They were suspended from trading due to a pipeline disruption.
They reached a record peak of 2,519 trillion Australian dollars.
questions.e: Gold equities suffered sharp losses as the Federal Reserve rate hike altered sector valuations, with Bellevue Gold trading at AUD 1.54 and Metallium dropping 4.35%. Financials rallied, but gold stocks fell.

questions.q: Which organization claimed responsibility for the attacks targeting a Saudi Aramco facility and a strategic air base?
o: Yemen's Houthis executed coordinated missile and drone strikes against the facilities.
Indian refiners launched kinetic operations following pipeline disruptions.
European oil cargo buyers carried out coordinated drone strikes over replacement costs.
State oil producers in Nigeria launched missile strikes to protest high fuel prices.
questions.e: Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility for missile and drone strikes targeting a Saudi Aramco facility and an air base.
